title.narrative: Output 7.3. Increased capacity of member States to set adequate wages and promote decent working time

description.narrative: The Parliament has amended the Employment Act with the effect that sectoral minimum wage orders must be issued and implemented, starting in 2021. In setting minimum wages, both needs of workers and their families and economic factors must be taken into account. It is the first time that the Maldives will implement a minimum wage system. In the process, the Ministry of Economic Development provided a robust evidence base through the publication in February 2020 of the first Report of the Salaries and Wage Advisory Board (created in 2019) on setting minimum wages in the Maldives. Furthermore, in May 2021, after some delays due to the COVID-19 situation, the Ministry of Economic Development has expanded the Salaries and Wage Board in the Maldives with additional stakeholders, while also appointing a new Chairman, to strengthen consultation on the adoption of the new minimum wage system. Since 2019, following an official request from the Minister of Economic Development of the Maldives, the ILO has provided technical assistance to recommend a methodology and set a national minimum wage for the first time. The Salaries and Wage Advisory Board and its Secretariat worked arduously with ILO to assess and collect the available data and information to conduct the study to develop a methodology to determine the minimum wage in the country. The final outcome came through a report owned by the SWAB and published by the Ministry of Economic Development in Februrary 2020. The report addressed the possibility to have a national and/or seven sectoral minimum wages. https://www.trade.gov.mv/reports-publications The COVID-19 pandemic pressured Government to postpone the decision for setting the minimum wage in 2020. According to the newly amended Employment Act it has been established that the minimum wage would be implemented in 2021. A consultation between the new chairperson of the Salaries and Wages Board, the Minister of State for Economic Development and the ILO was held on June 29, 2021. The chairman briefed the ILO on the updates of the evidence-based process, and the inclusion of two new sectors for setting the minimum wage. The sectors include and Fisheries and Agriculture, Tourism, Construction, Transport, Health, Education, Small and Medium Enterprises, Communication and Technology and Information. The ILO provided advice on technical matters and re-emphasised the importance of implementing the minimum wage system in the Maldives. ILO confirmed that the process has been strengthened under the expanded Salaries and Wage Board and assured that technical assistance could be further provided once the minimum wages are established and the minimum wage implementation begins.
